Later, in 807, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro built the shrine's current structure, with Japanese Emperor Yamato Takeru's enshrinement following the deity in 1625 during the construction of Tanakura Castle. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Takamatsu family. In the early Edo period, the shrine was relocated from the Tanakura Castle site to its current location. In the Meiji period, the shrine was recognized as a Kokuhosha and later became a Beppyo Shrine. ===境内=== [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, reconstructed by Satake Yoshinobu in 1594 and moved to its current location in 1625, is a three-bay Nagare-zukuri style structure with a copper roof. The hall is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. {{Short description|Shrine in Tanakura, Fukushima, Japan}} [[ja:都々古別神社]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|thumb]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|thumb]] '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, ''Tsutsukowake jinja'') is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Tanagura, Fukushima]] Prefecture, Japan. It was the [[ichinomiya]] of [[Mutsu Province]]. According to legend, it was founded in 807. ==Overview== {{Double image stack|right|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|280|{{Center|Top: Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Tanakura)
Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} {{coordinates list}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine

{{Short description|Shrine in Tanakura, Fukushima, Japan}} [[ja:都々古別神社]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|thumb]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|thumb]] '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, ''Tsutsukowake jinja'') is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Tanagura, Fukushima]] Prefecture, Japan. It was the [[ichinomiya]] of [[Mutsu Province]]. According to legend, it was founded in 807. ==Overview== {{Double image stack|right|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|280|{{Center|Top: Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Tanakura)
Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} {{coordinates list}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine
（Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine） |image = [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) haiden.JPG|270px]]
Haiden (Worship Hall) |address = [[Fukushima Prefecture]][[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], Baba 39 |coordinates = {{Coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E|region:JP-07_type:landmark|display=inline|name=Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)}} |deity = [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] |rank = [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (Myojin Taisha)]], [[Ichinomiya]], Former [[Kokuhosha]] of the Second rank, [[Beppyo Shrine]] |established = Legend: Year 807 |main hall = Three-bay Nagare-zukuri |alternative name = Baba Myojin |札所等 = Chikatsu Sansha |reisai= September 11 |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|22|33.30|label=Tsutsukowake Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}}} }} ===deity=== The enshrined deities are: * Main deity: [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] * Co-deity: [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]] ===History=== ====Establishment==== According to the shrine's records, Prince Yamato Takeru enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto on Mount Kenkobu during Emperor Keikō's reign. Later, in 807, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro built the shrine's current structure, with Japanese Emperor Yamato Takeru's enshrinement following the deity in 1625 during the construction of Tanakura Castle. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Takamatsu family. In the early Edo period, the shrine was relocated from the Tanakura Castle site to its current location. In the Meiji period, the shrine was recognized as a Kokuhosha and later became a Beppyo Shrine. ===境内=== [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, reconstructed by Satake Yoshinobu in 1594 and moved to its current location in 1625, is a three-bay Nagare-zukuri style structure with a copper roof. The hall is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-2.JPG|Shrine Buildings File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) zuishinmon.JPG|Zuishin Gate File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) entrance.JPG|Second Torii File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) torii.JPG|Main Torii ===Associated Shrines=== * Koyama Tenmangu Shrine - Enshrines Sugawara no Michizane * Inari Shrine * Itsukushima Shrine * Kashima Shrine * Shinmei Shrine * Toshogu Shrine * Hie Shrine * Kumano Shrine * Torausu Shrine ===annual festivals=== The shrine's annual events include: * Monthly festival (11th of each month) * New Year's festival (January 1) * Setsubun festival (February 3) * Prayer festival (February 17) * Tenjin Lecture (March 25) * Kagura Lecture festival (May 1) * Great Purification festival (June 30) * '''Main festival''' (September 11) * Niiname festival (November 23) * Great Purification festival (December 31) ===Cultural Properties=== ====National Important Cultural Property==== * main hall (designated on December 10, 2014) * Long-ridged Sword (located at Shirakawa Shukokan Museum, designated on April 30, 1921) * Red-stringed Armor (early Kamakura period, designated on February 19, 1957) ====Fukushima Prefecture Cultural Property==== * Important Cultural Property (designated on March 30, 1982) * Sword-shaped Ritual Items (designated on March 25, 2003) * Shrine Documents (designated on April 15, 2005) ===location=== '''address:''' * 39 Baba, Tanakura, Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima, Japan '''Access:''' * A 15-minute walk from JR East Suigun Line's Iwaki-Tanakura Station == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine
（Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine） |image = [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) haiden.JPG|270px]]

[[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]] |rank = [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (Myojin Taisha)]], [[Ichinomiya]], Former [[Kokuhosha]] of the Second rank, [[Beppyo Shrine]] |established = Legend: Emperor Keikō's Reign, or 811 |main hall = Nagare-zukuri |alternative name = Yatsuki Myojin, Chikatsu Myojin |札所等 = Chikatsu Sansha |reisai= Second Saturday and Sunday of December (Shimotsuki festival) |festival = [[Tsutsukowake Shrine Rice-Planting ceremony|Rice-Planting festival]] (January 6) |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|label=Tsutsukowake Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}}} }} ===deity=== The enshrined deities are: * [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] * [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]] ===History=== ====Establishment==== According to the shrine's records, Prince Yamato Takeru enshrined three protective deities on Mount Kenkobu during Emperor Keikō's reign. Later, the shrine was established where one of the arrows fired by Yamato Takeru landed, and the shrine was named "Yatsuki." The shrine's name was changed to "Chikatsu Myojin" by Minamoto no Yoshiie during his campaign in Oshu. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Yatsuki family. Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} {{coordinates list}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine

Later, in 807, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro built the shrine's current structure, with Japanese Emperor Yamato Takeru's enshrinement following the deity in 1625 during the construction of Tanakura Castle. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Takamatsu family. In the early Edo period, the shrine was relocated from the Tanakura Castle site to its current location. In the Meiji period, the shrine was recognized as a Kokuhosha and later became a Beppyo Shrine. ===境内=== [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, reconstructed by Satake Yoshinobu in 1594 and moved to its current location in 1625, is a three-bay Nagare-zukuri style structure with a copper roof. The hall is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. {{Short description|Shrine in Tanakura, Fukushima, Japan}} [[ja:都々古別神社]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|thumb]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|thumb]] '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, ''Tsutsukowake jinja'') is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Tanagura, Fukushima]] Prefecture, Japan. It was the [[ichinomiya]] of [[Mutsu Province]]. According to legend, it was founded in 807. ==Overview== {{Double image stack|right|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|280|{{Center|Top: Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Tanakura)
Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} {{coordinates list}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine

{{Short description|Shrine in Tanakura, Fukushima, Japan}} [[ja:都々古別神社]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|thumb]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|thumb]] '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, ''Tsutsukowake jinja'') is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Tanagura, Fukushima]] Prefecture, Japan. It was the [[ichinomiya]] of [[Mutsu Province]]. According to legend, it was founded in 807. ==Overview== {{Double image stack|right|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|280|{{Center|Top: Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Tanakura)
Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} {{coordinates list}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine
（Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine） |image = [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) haiden.JPG|270px]]
Haiden (Worship Hall) |address = [[Fukushima Prefecture]][[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], Baba 39 |coordinates = {{Coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E|region:JP-07_type:landmark|display=inline|name=Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)}} |deity = [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] |rank = [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (Myojin Taisha)]], [[Ichinomiya]], Former [[Kokuhosha]] of the Second rank, [[Beppyo Shrine]] |established = Legend: Year 807 |main hall = Three-bay Nagare-zukuri |alternative name = Baba Myojin |札所等 = Chikatsu Sansha |festival= September 11 |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|22|33.30|label=Tsutsukowake Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}}} }} ===deity=== The enshrined deities are: * Main deity: [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] * Co-deity: [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]] ===History=== ====Establishment==== According to the shrine's records, Prince Yamato Takeru enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto on Mount Kenkobu during Emperor Keikō's reign. Later, in 807, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro built the shrine's current structure, with Japanese Emperor Yamato Takeru's enshrinement following the deity in 1625 during the construction of Tanakura Castle. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Takamatsu family. In the early Edo period, the shrine was relocated from the Tanakura Castle site to its current location. In the Meiji period, the shrine was recognized as a Kokuhosha and later became a Beppyo Shrine. ===境内=== [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, reconstructed by Satake Yoshinobu in 1594 and moved to its current location in 1625, is a three-bay Nagare-zukuri style structure with a copper roof. The hall is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-2.JPG|Shrine Buildings File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) zuishinmon.JPG|Zuishin Gate File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) entrance.JPG|Second Torii File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) torii.JPG|Main Torii ===Associated Shrines=== * Koyama Tenmangu Shrine - Enshrines Sugawara no Michizane * Inari Shrine * Itsukushima Shrine * Kashima Shrine * Shinmei Shrine * Toshogu Shrine * Hie Shrine * Kumano Shrine * Torausu Shrine ===annual festivals=== The shrine's annual events include: * Monthly festival (11th of each month) * New Year's festival (January 1) * Setsubun festival (February 3) * Prayer festival (February 17) * Tenjin Lecture (March 25) * Kagura Lecture festival (May 1) * Great Purification festival (June 30) * '''Main festival''' (September 11) * Niiname festival (November 23) * Great Purification festival (December 31) ===Cultural Properties=== ====National Important Cultural Property==== * main hall (designated on December 10, 2014) * Long-ridged Sword (located at Shirakawa Shukokan Museum, designated on April 30, 1921) * Red-stringed Armor (early Kamakura period, designated on February 19, 1957) ====Fukushima Prefecture Cultural Property==== * Important Cultural Property (designated on March 30, 1982) * Sword-shaped Ritual Items (designated on March 25, 2003) * Shrine Documents (designated on April 15, 2005) ===location=== '''address:''' * 39 Baba, Tanakura, Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima, Japan '''Access:''' * A 15-minute walk from JR East Suigun Line's Iwaki-Tanakura Station == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine

Later, the shrine was established where one of the arrows fired by Yamato Takeru landed, and the shrine was named "Yatsuki." The shrine's name was changed to "Chikatsu Myojin" by Minamoto no Yoshiie during his campaign in Oshu. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine

{{Short description|Shrine in Tanakura, Fukushima, Japan}} [[ja:都々古別神社]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|thumb]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|thumb]] '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, ''Tsutsukowake jinja'') is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Tanagura, Fukushima]] Prefecture, Japan. It was the [[ichinomiya]] of [[Mutsu Province]]. According to legend, it was founded in 807. ==Overview== {{Double image stack|right|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|280|{{Center|Top: Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Tanakura)
Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine

{{Short description|Shrine in Tanakura, Fukushima, Japan}} [[ja:都々古別神社]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|thumb]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|thumb]] '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, ''Tsutsukowake jinja'') is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Tanagura, Fukushima]] Prefecture, Japan. It was the [[ichinomiya]] of [[Mutsu Province]]. According to legend, it was founded in 807. ==Overview== {{Double image stack|right|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|280|{{Center|Top: Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Tanakura)
Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine
（Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine） |image = [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) haiden.JPG|270px]]
Haiden (Worship Hall) |location = [[Fukushima Prefecture]][[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], Baba 39 |coordinates = {{Coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E|region:JP-07_type:landmark|display=inline|name=Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)}} |deity = [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] |rank = [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (Myojin Taisha)]], [[Ichinomiya]], Former [[Kokuhosha]] of the Second rank, [[Beppyo Shrine]] |established = Legend: Year 807 |main hall = Three-bay Nagare-zukuri |alternative name = Baba Myojin |札所等 = Chikatsu Sansha |festival= September 11 |map = {{location map|Japan Fukushima|lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|22|33.30|label=Tsutsukowake Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}}} }} ===deity=== The enshrined deities are: * Main deity: [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] * Co-deity: [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]] ===History=== ====Establishment==== According to the shrine's records, Prince Yamato Takeru enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto on Mount Kenkobu during Emperor Keikō's reign. Later, in 807, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro built the shrine's current structure, with Japanese Emperor Yamato Takeru's enshrinement following the deity in 1625 during the construction of Tanakura Castle. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Takamatsu family. In the early Edo period, the shrine was relocated from the Tanakura Castle site to its current location. In the Meiji period, the shrine was recognized as a Kokuhosha and later became a Beppyo Shrine. ===境内=== [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, reconstructed by Satake Yoshinobu in 1594 and moved to its current location in 1625, is a three-bay Nagare-zukuri style structure with a copper roof. The hall is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-2.JPG|Shrine Buildings File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) zuishinmon.JPG|Zuishin Gate File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) entrance.JPG|Second Torii File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) torii.JPG|Main Torii ===Associated Shrines=== * Koyama Tenmangu Shrine - Enshrines Sugawara no Michizane * Inari Shrine * Itsukushima Shrine * Kashima Shrine * Shinmei Shrine * Toshogu Shrine * Hie Shrine * Kumano Shrine * Torausu Shrine ===festivals=== The shrine's annual events include: * Monthly festival (11th of each month) * New Year's festival (January 1) * Setsubun festival (February 3) * Prayer festival (February 17) * Tenjin Lecture (March 25) * Kagura Lecture festival (May 1) * Great Purification festival (June 30) * '''Main festival''' (September 11) * Niiname festival (November 23) * Great Purification festival (December 31) ===Cultural Properties=== ====National Important Cultural Property==== * main hall (designated on December 10, 2014) * Long-ridged Sword (located at Shirakawa Shukokan Museum, designated on April 30, 1921) * Red-stringed Armor (early Kamakura period, designated on February 19, 1957) ====Fukushima Prefecture Cultural Property==== * Important Cultural Property (designated on March 30, 1982) * Sword-shaped Ritual Items (designated on March 25, 2003) * Shrine Documents (designated on April 15, 2005) ===location=== '''location:''' * 39 Baba, Tanakura, Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima, Japan '''Access:''' * A 15-minute walk from JR East Suigun Line's Iwaki-Tanakura Station == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine

Later, the shrine was established where one of the arrows fired by Yamato Takeru landed, and the shrine was named "Yatsuki." The shrine's name was changed to "Chikatsu Myojin" by Minamoto no Yoshiie during his campaign in Oshu. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Yatsuki family. It was the [[ichinomiya]] of [[Mutsu Province]]. According to legend, it was founded in 807. ==Overview== {{Double image stack|right|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|280|{{Center|Top: Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Tanakura)
Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine

Later, in 807, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro built the shrine's current structure, with Japanese Emperor Yamato Takeru's enshrinement following the deity in 1625 during the construction of Tanakura Castle. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Takamatsu family. In the early Edo period, the shrine was relocated from the Tanakura Castle site to its current location. In the Meiji period, the shrine was recognized as a Kokuhosha and later became a Beppyo Shrine. ===境内=== [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, reconstructed by Satake Yoshinobu in 1594 and moved to its current location in 1625, is a three-bay Nagare-zukuri style structure with a copper roof. The hall is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. Later, the shrine was established where one of the arrows fired by Yamato Takeru landed, and the shrine was named "Yatsuki." The shrine's name was changed to "Chikatsu Myojin" by Minamoto no Yoshiie during his campaign in Oshu. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. Later, in 807, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro built the shrine's current structure, with Japanese Emperor Yamato Takeru's enshrinement following the deity in 1625 during the construction of Tanakura Castle. ====Historical Significance==== The shrine is recognized as one of the proposed sites listed in the Engishiki. During the medieval period, it incorporated Shugendo elements and was managed by the Takamatsu family. In the early Edo period, the shrine was relocated from the Tanakura Castle site to its current location. In the Meiji period, the shrine was recognized as a Kokuhosha and later became a Beppyo Shrine. ===境内=== [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, reconstructed by Satake Yoshinobu in 1594 and moved to its current location in 1625, is a three-bay Nagare-zukuri style structure with a copper roof. The hall is designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. {{Short description|Shrine in Tanakura, Fukushima, Japan}} [[Category:dd]][[ja:都々古別神社]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|thumb]] [[File:Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|thumb]] '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, ''Tsutsukowake jinja'') is a [[Shinto]] shrine located in [[Tanagura, Fukushima]] Prefecture, Japan. It was the [[ichinomiya]] of [[Mutsu Province]]. According to legend, it was founded in 807. ==Overview== {{Double image stack|right|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Baba) shaden-1.JPG|Tsutsukowake-jinja (Yatsuki) zuishinmon-1.JPG|280|{{Center|Top: Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Tanakura)
Bottom: Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki)}}}} {{location map+|Japan Fukushima |width=280|float=right|caption={{center|locations of Baba Shrine, Yatsuki Shrine, and related shrines}}|places= {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=1|lat_sec=55.46|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=33.30|position=top|label_size=95|label=Baba Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=59|lat_sec=40.31|lon_deg=140|lon_min=23|lon_sec=31.56|position=right|label_size=95|label=Yatsuki Shrine|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=10}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=37|lat_min=3|lat_sec=14.75|lon_deg=140|lon_min=19|lon_sec=42.94|position=left|label_size=85|label=Kenkobu-san|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} {{location map~|Japan Fukushima |lat_deg=36|lat_min=49|lat_sec=6.48|lon_deg=140|lon_min=22|lon_sec=10.76|position=left|label_size=85|label=Chikatsu Shrine|mark=Blue pog.svg|marksize=8}} }} {{OSM location map|coord={{coord|37.019429|N|140.387609|E}}|fullscreen-option=0|zoom=12|float=right|width=280|caption=|title=|mark-coord1={{coord|37|1|55.46|N|140|22|33.30|E}}|label1=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos1=top|mark-size1=8|mark-coord2={{coord|36|59|40.31|N|140|23|31.56|E}}|label2=Tsutsukowake Shrine|label-pos2=bottom|mark-size2=8}} '''Tsutsukowake Shrine''' (都々古別神社, Tsutsukowake Jinja) is a Shinto shrine located in [[Tanakura, Fukushima|Tanakura Town]], [[Higashishirakawa District, Fukushima|Higashishirakawa District]], [[Fukushima Prefecture]]. There are two main shrines with the same name, both of which are historical shrines in the former [[Mutsu Province]] [[Shikinaisha|and are considered to be Ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrines) of the province]]. == Overview == The two main shrines known as Tsutsukowake Shrine are both listed as [[Shikinaisha|Shikinaisha (official shrines listed in the Engishiki laws)]] and are each recognized as Ichinomiya of Mutsu Province. They are: # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Tanakura) - Former [[Kokuhosha|National Shrine of the Second rank]], and [[Beppyo Shrine]]. # '''[[#Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Yatsuki)|Tsutsukowake Shrine (Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine)]]''' (Tanakura Town, Yatsuki) - Former Kokuhosha of the Second rank, and Beppyo Shrine. Both shrines enshrine [[Ajisukitakahikone|Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto]] and [[Yamato Takeru|Yamato Takeru no Mikoto]]. The exact historical relationships between these two shrines and their relation to the official Tsutsukowake Shrine listed in the Engishiki remains a topic of historical debate. These shrines, along with [[Chikatsu Shrine (Daigo, Shimo))|Chikatsu Shrine]] in [[Daigo, Ibaraki|Daigo Town]], [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], are collectively known as the "Chikatsu Sansha" (Three Chikatsu Shrines). The numerous shrines in the southern Mutsu region, which include "Tsutsukowake" or "Chikatsu" in their names or enshrine Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto, indicate the widespread influence of these shrines in the area. == Shrine names == Historically, the shrine names have been recorded as: * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the year 841 in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" * Tsutsukowake Shrine (都都古和氣神社) in the "Engishiki" and temporary rituals * Tsutsukowake no Kami (都々古和気神) in the "Chōyō Gunzai" The origin of the name "Tsutsukowake" is debated, with theories including references to the revered straw bag "Tsutsuko" or connections to drum-like objects or derivations from the deity Chikatsu in Suwa, Nagano. Another shrine with a similar name, Ishitsutsukowake Shrine, is also listed in the "Engishiki" for Mutsu Province, located in [[Ishikawa Town]], [[Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Ishikawa District]], Fukushima. During the medieval and early modern periods, the Baba shrine was known as "Baba Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin," and the Yatsuki shrine was known as "Yatsuki Myojin" or "Chikatsu Myojin (Chikatsu Myojin)." In the Meiji period and beyond, both shrines took on the name "Tsutsukowake Shrine," with distinctions as "Baba Tsutsukowake Shrine" and "Yatsuki Tsutsukowake Shrine." == History == === Establishment === Both the Baba and Yatsuki shrines claim origins during the reign of Emperor Keikō (12th Emperor) with legends involving Prince Yamato Takeru, who reached the Oshu region and enshrined Ajisukitakahikone no Mikoto as a guardian deity on Mount Kenkobu (建鉾山). These legends describe various relocations and reestablishments of the shrines. The Kenkobu Mountain site is known as a significant ancient ritual site from the 5th century, and modern interpretations link the shrine's establishment to the creation of a new road between Mutsu and Hitachi around the year 811. ==== Historical Records ==== The first historical record appears in the "Zoku Nihon Kōki" in 841, mentioning "Tsutsukowake no Kami." The "Engishiki" records list it as a Myojin Taisha (Great Shine) in Mutsu Province's Shirakawa District. During the medieval period, both shrines adopted Shugendo (mountain worship) practices. Baba Shrine was initially located at Tanakura Castle before relocating to its current site in 1625. Both shrines were officially recognized as Kokuhosha (National Shrines) in the Meiji period, with Baba Shrine achieving this status in 1873 and Yatsuki Shrine following in 1885. Post-World War II, both shrines are listed as Beppyo Shrines under the Association of Shinto Shrines. == Tsutsukowake Shrine (Tanakura Town Tanakura) == {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Tsutsukowake Shrine
